mainTopic: ט״ו באב's joyful reasons, the seven lives spanning history, who was under the desert decree, and how ארץ ישראל was divided
overview: The גמרא finishes listing reasons why ט״ו באב became a happy day. It shows from the order of two פסוקים that God spoke to משה again only after the desert generation stopped dying. Then come more reasons: the roads to ירושלים were reopened by הושע בן אלה, the dead of ביתר were buried (when הטוב והמטיב was set up in יבנה), and the wood-cutting for the מזבח ended, a day nicknamed ׳יום תבר מגל׳. Since the nights grow longer from then on, one who adds Torah learning at night adds to his life. Next a ברייתא lists seven people whose lives cover all of history, from אדם to אליהו. The גמרא asks how אחיה השילוני could have survived the desert. רב המנונא answers that שבט לוי was not under the decree, but this is challenged from יאיר בן מנשה, who also lived on. So רב אחא בר יעקב rules that the decree covered only people aged twenty to sixty. Finally the גמרא asks whether ארץ ישראל was divided by tribe or by head count, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from a פסוק that God spoke to משה again only after the dying ended
steps.stepSummary: Finishing the earlier reason for ט״ו באב, the גמרא shows from the order of the פסוקים in דברים that God's speech came back to משה only after the last of the desert generation had died.
steps.simpleTranslation: God did not speak with משה, as it says: 'And it was, when all the men of war had finished dying from among the people,' and right next to it: 'The Lord spoke to me, saying.' Only then was the speech to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing an explanation that started before this section: ט״ו באב is the day the desert generation stopped dying. It proves that the dying had paused God's close speech with משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים stand side by side: one says the men of war finished dying, and the next says God spoke to משה. Because they are placed next to each other, the גמרא learns that God's direct speech to משה came back only once the dying was over. That return showed the decree had ended, which is why the day became a day of joy.

keyTerms.meaning: Divine speech, God speaking to a נביא
And right next to it (a lesson learned from two פסוקים placed side by side)
The men of war, meaning the generation that left מצרים

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand new opinion. It is the end of an explanation the גמרא already started before this section.

phrases.english: There was no speech of God with Moses,
as it says: 'And it was, when they finished,
all the men of war, dying
from among the people,'
and right next to it is written:
'The Lord spoke to me, saying'
only then was the speech directed to me.
phrases.notes: This is משה speaking: only once the dying stopped did God speak to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an explanation of ט״ו באב that began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that God did not speak with משה while the desert generation was dying.

steps.title: עולא: the day the roads to ירושלים were reopened
steps.stepSummary: עולא gives a different reason: ט״ו באב is the day הושע בן אלה removed the guards that ירבעם had placed on the roads to stop people from going up for the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is the day when הושע בן אלה removed the guards that ירבעם had placed on the roads so that ישראל would not go up for the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, separate explanation for why ט״ו באב is a happy day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירבעם had blocked the roads to keep people from going up to ירושלים for the festivals. On ט״ו באב, הושע בן אלה took those guards away, so people could go up again. Reopening the way to the בית המקדש was a reason to celebrate.

keyTerms.meaning: Guards or guard posts
For the pilgrimage festival, going up to ירושלים
Cancelled, removed

phrases.english: Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם שֶׁבִּיטֵּל בּוֹ הוֹשֵׁעַ בֶּן אֵלָה
phrases.english: It is the day on which Hoshea son of Elah removed
the guards that Jeroboam had stationed on the roads,
so that Israel would not go up for the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reason for the joy of ט״ו באב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב celebrates the day הושע בן אלה removed ירבעם's road guards and let the people go up to ירושלים again.

steps.title: רב מתנה: the day the dead of ביתר were buried
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה says ט״ו באב is the day the people killed at ביתר were finally allowed to be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: It is the day when the slain of ביתר were given over for burial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third explanation for the joy of ט״ו באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people killed at ביתר had been left unburied. The day they were finally allowed burial was a day of comfort and thanks, so it became a happy day.

keyTerms.meaning: Those killed in the destruction of the city ביתר
For burial

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
It is the day when the slain of Beitar were given over for burial.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב marks the day the dead of ביתר were allowed burial.

steps.title: The blessing הטוב והמטיב was set up on that same day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up רב מתנה with another statement of his: on the day of the burial of ביתר, the חכמים in יבנה set up the ברכה of הטוב והמטיב, with each word matching a different kindness.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב מתנה said: On the day the slain of ביתר were given over for burial, they instituted in יבנה הטוב והמטיב, 'Who is good and Who does good.' הטוב: that the bodies did not rot. והמטיב: that they were given over for burial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how important that burial day was by quoting רב מתנה's other statement that a ברכה was set up because of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the burial was such a big event that a lasting ברכה was set up for it. The two words of the ברכה match two miracles: הטוב, because the bodies did not rot over the long wait, and והמטיב, because they were finally buried.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who is good and Who does good', a ברכה of thanks
They set up, instituted (a rabbinic enactment)
יבנה, the seat of the חכמים after the חורבן
Rotted, decayed

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source given here for the ברכה of הטוב והמטיב, which is part of ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: As Rav Mattana said:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ הֲרוּגֵי בֵיתָר לִקְבוּרָה –
phrases.english: On that day when the slain of Beitar were given over for burial,
they instituted in Yavne 'Who is good and Who does good.'
'Who is good': that they did not rot,
'and Who does good': that they were given over for burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב מתנה's reason with another statement of his.
steps.raayaObject: That the burial of the dead of ביתר was a major day worth celebrating.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב מתנה's statement that הטוב והמטיב was set up in יבנה on that day.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף: the day wood-cutting for the מזבח stopped
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף both say ט״ו באב is the day they stopped cutting wood for the wood pile on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both said: It is the day on which they stop cutting wood for the altar arrangement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth explanation for ט״ו באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting wood for the מזבח was a big yearly job. Finishing it on ט״ו באב was a celebration, like the end of a harvest.

keyTerms.meaning: The arranged wood pile on the מזבח
Stop, cease
Both of them

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef, who both said:
It is the day on which they stop
cutting wood for the altar arrangement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another separate reason for ט״ו באב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב is the day the cutting of wood for the מערכה ended for the year.

steps.title: A ברייתא: after ט״ו באב the sun weakens and wood is not cut
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר הגדול supports רבה and רב יוסף: from ט״ו באב the sun gets weaker, and they would no longer cut wood for the מערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר the Great says: Once the fifteenth of Av arrived, the strength of the sun weakened, and they would not cut wood for the altar arrangement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to prove that wood-cutting really did stop on ט״ו באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the reason for the date: after ט״ו באב the sun is weaker. The usual explanation is that wood cut after that would not dry well enough for the מזבח, so the cutting season ended that day.

keyTerms.meaning: Its strength weakened
The sun

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
Once the fifteenth of Av arrived,
the strength of the sun weakened,
and they would not cut wood for the altar arrangement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה and רב יוסף from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That wood-cutting for the מערכה ended on ט״ו באב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אליעזר הגדול.

steps.title: רב מנשה: the day was called ׳the day the sickle breaks׳
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשה adds that people called ט״ו באב ׳יום תבר מגל׳, the day of breaking the sickle, since the cutting tools were no longer needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשה said: And they called it ׳יום תבר מגל׳, 'the day of breaking the sickle.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשה adds a popular nickname for ט״ו באב that fits the wood-cutting explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name shows that this day was widely known as the end of the cutting season. 'Breaking the sickle' means the tools were put aside until the next year.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking (Aramaic)
Sickle, a cutting tool
They called it

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא gives several reasons for the joy of ט״ו באב: the desert dying ended, the roads to ירושלים reopened, the dead of ביתר were buried (source of הטוב והמטיב), and the wood-cutting for the מזבח was finished (׳יום תבר מגל׳).

phrases.english: Rav Menashe said:
And they called it 'the day of breaking the sickle.'
phrases.notes: The cutting tools were 'broken', meaning put away, since no more wood was cut that year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a popular name that fits the wood-cutting explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב was popularly called ׳יום תבר מגל׳.

steps.title: From ט״ו באב on, adding night learning adds life
steps.stepSummary: From ט״ו באב onward, one who adds Torah learning at night will have his life added to, and one who does not add is called ׳יסיף׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here onward, whoever adds will be added to, and whoever does not add, ׳יסיף׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a final lesson about ט״ו באב. Since the nights start getting longer, a person should use them to learn more Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said the sun gets weaker from ט״ו באב, so the nights grow longer. The גמרא turns that fact into a lesson: adding learning at night brings a longer life. It also uses a hard word, ׳יסיף׳, for the one who does not add. Step 9 asks what it means, and step 10 answers.

keyTerms.meaning: from here onward, meaning from ט״ו באב on
one who adds, here meaning adding Torah learning at night
will add, meaning years will be added to his life
an unclear word for the one who does not add; it is explained in the next steps

phrases.english: From here onward,
phrases.notes: He means from ט״ו באב, when the nights start getting longer.

phrases.english: one who adds will be added to,
phrases.notes: Adds Torah learning at night, and years get added to his life.

phrases.english: one who does not add is ׳yesif׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the weakening sun of step 6 and the end of wood cutting in step 7. Longer nights should be used for learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From ט״ו באב on, adding night learning lengthens life, and not adding brings the result called ׳יסיף׳.

steps.title: What does ׳יסיף׳ mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unusual word ׳יסיף׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the strange word ׳יסיף׳ means. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is not a normal Hebrew word, so the warning in step 8 is unclear. The גמרא needs to know exactly what happens to a person who does not add learning.

keyTerms.meaning: what is it? (asking for a meaning)

phrases.english: What does ׳yesif׳ mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the last word of step 8.

steps.title: His mother will bury him
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that ׳יסיף׳ means his mother will bury him, so he will die young.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: his mother will bury him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. ׳יסיף׳ means the person will die while his mother is still alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of ׳יוסיף׳. One who adds learning gets more years, and one who does not loses years and dies before his own mother.

keyTerms.meaning: his mother will bury him

steps.whatToRemember: From ט״ו באב the nights grow longer. Adding Torah learning then adds life, and not adding cuts life short.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
his mother will bury him.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ׳יסיף׳ means his mother will bury him, so he will die early.

steps.title: Seven people whose lives cover all of history
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that seven people, each of whom saw the one before, cover all of history from אדם until today, since אליהו is still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: seven people spanned the whole world. מתושלח saw אדם, שם saw מתושלח, יעקב saw שם, עמרם saw יעקב, אחיה השילוני saw עמרם, and אליהו saw אחיה השילוני, and he is still alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a chain of seven people. Each one was alive at the same time as the one before him, so together they reach from אדם until now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each link only works if the two lives overlapped. The link between עמרם and אחיה השילוני is the one that will cause trouble in the next step. The chain ends with אליהו, who never died, so it reaches all the way to the present.

keyTerms.meaning: folded up, meaning their lives spanned the whole span of history
Ahiyah from Shiloh, a נביא
and he is still alive

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁבְעָה קִפְּלוּ אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ –
phrases.english: Seven people spanned the whole entire world:
phrases.notes: Literally 'folded up the world'. Their lifetimes, one after another, cover all of history.

phrases.english: Methushelach saw Adam,
Shem saw Methushelach,
Yaakov saw Shem,
Amram saw Yaakov,
Ahiyah HaShiloni saw Amram,
Eliyahu saw Ahiyah HaShiloni,
and he is still alive.
phrases.notes: This is אליהו, who never died.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁבְעָה קִפְּלוּ אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, a chain of long lives across history.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven overlapping lives connect all of history: אדם, מתושלח, שם, יעקב, עמרם, אחיה השילוני, אליהו.

steps.title: How could אחיה השילוני have seen עמרם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the link between עמרם and אחיה השילוני from a פסוק saying that only כלב and יהושע survived the desert.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did אחיה השילוני really see עמרם? But it is written: ״And not a man of them was left, except כלב בן יפנה and יהושע בן נון״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks one link in the chain. If אחיה was old enough to see עמרם, he was a grown man when they left מצרים, and the פסוק says all those men died in the desert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עמרם died before the people left מצרים, so אחיה must have been an adult at that time. The פסוק says no one from that group survived except כלב and יהושע. Then אחיה could not have lived on to later times, where אליהו could see him.

keyTerms.meaning: but it is written! (introduces a challenge from a פסוק)
was left, survived
Calev son of Yefuneh, one of the two who survived

phrases.english: And did Ahiyah HaShiloni see Amram?
But it is written:
״And not a man of them was left,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִם כָּלֵב בֶּן יְפֻנֶּה וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן״!
phrases.english: except Calev son of Yefuneh and Yehoshua son of Nun״!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲחִיָּה הַשִּׁילוֹנִי רָאָה אֶת עַמְרָם? וְהָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one link (עמרם to אחיה) in the chain of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that אחיה השילוני saw עמרם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: To see עמרם, אחיה had to be an adult at יציאת מצרים. The פסוק says all of those people died in the desert except כלב and יהושע, so אחיה could not have lived on.

steps.title: The desert decree did not include שבט לוי
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא answers that the decree to die in the desert was only on those counted from age twenty, and שבט לוי was counted from age thirty, so it was not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: The decree was not made on שבט לוי, as it is written: ״In this desert your bodies will fall, and all those counted of you, by your full number, from twenty years old and up״. This means those counted from twenty, which leaves out שבט לוי, who were counted from thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא answers the challenge. He shows from the פסוק that the decree to die in the desert never covered שבט לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree in the פסוק only covers people whose census started at age twenty. שבט לוי was counted from age thirty, so it was outside the decree. The answer assumes אחיה was from שבט לוי, so he could survive the desert and the chain stays standing.

keyTerms.meaning: decree, here the decree to die in the desert
his counting, the age from which his tribe was counted
the tribe of לוי
is left out, excluded

steps.whatToRemember: רב המנונא's answer: the decree covered only those counted from age twenty, so שבט לוי, counted from thirty, was not included, and a לוי like אחיה השילוני could live on. Steps 14-16 challenge this answer and replace it with a new one.
steps.confusionAlert: The question in the previous step was not about the whole chain. It was only about whether אחיה could have survived the desert, and this answer fixes only that link.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִגְזְרָה גְּזֵרָה עַל שִׁבְטוֹ שֶׁל לֵוִי,
phrases.english: The decree was not made on the tribe of Levi,
as it is written:
״In this desert your bodies will fall,
and all those counted of you, by your full number,
from twenty years old and up״.
This means one whose counting is from age twenty,
which leaves out the tribe of Levi,
whose counting is from age thirty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: לֹא נִגְזְרָה גְּזֵרָה עַל שִׁבְטוֹ שֶׁל לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by narrowing who the desert decree covered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the decree using the wording of a different פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone who was an adult at יציאת מצרים died in the desert, so אחיה could not have survived.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only those counted from age twenty were under the decree. שבט לוי, counted from thirty, was not, so אחיה could survive.

steps.title: Challenge: יאיר and מכיר from שבט מנשה also entered the land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that only שבט לוי escaped the decree. A ברייתא says יאיר בן מנשה and מכיר בן מנשה, born in יעקב's lifetime, lived until ישראל entered the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that nobody from the other tribes entered the land? But a ברייתא teaches that יאיר בן מנשה and מכיר בן מנשה were born in the days of יעקב and did not die until ישראל entered the land, as the פסוק says: 'And the men of העי struck about thirty-six men of them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב המנונא's answer. If only שבט לוי was spared, how could two men from שבט מנשה, who were adults during the desert years, have entered the land?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא said only שבט לוי was left out of the decree, so no adult from any other tribe except כלב and יהושע should have survived. The ברייתא names two men from שבט מנשה who lived through it. The פסוק about העי is the source the ברייתא gives, and the next step explains how it proves this.

keyTerms.meaning: The other tribes (all except לוי)
יאיר son of מנשה, a great man from שבט מנשה
The city of העי, where ישראל lost a battle in יהושע's time

phrases.english: And from the other tribes, nobody entered?
phrases.notes: This goes back to רב המנונא's answer that only שבט לוי was spared from the decree.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: יָאִיר בֶּן מְנַשֶּׁה וּמָכִיר בֶּן מְנַשֶּׁה
phrases.english: Yair son of Menashe and Machir son of Menashe
were born in the days of Yaakov,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מֵתוּ עַד שֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָאָרֶץ –
phrases.english: and they did not die until Israel entered the land,
as it is said: "And the men of Ai struck of them
about thirty-six men",

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב המנונא's answer from step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's claim that only שבט לוי was left out of the decree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא names adults from שבט מנשה who survived the desert, so the decree could not have covered every non-Levite adult.

steps.title: The פסוק about העי refers to יאיר בן מנשה
steps.stepSummary: A מחלוקת on the פסוק: רבי יהודה says exactly thirty-six died at העי. רבי נחמיה says 'about thirty-six' means יאיר בן מנשה alone, who was worth most of the סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: exactly thirty-six, the words of רבי יהודה. רבי נחמיה said to him: Does it say 'thirty-six'? It only says 'about thirty-six'! Rather, this is יאיר בן מנשה, who was equal to the majority of the סנהדרין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא to show how the פסוק of העי proves יאיר was still alive then. According to רבי נחמיה, the 'thirty-six' who fell at העי was really one man, יאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה focuses on the word 'about' (כ־) in the פסוק. It hints that the dead were not really thirty-six people but one person as important as thirty-six, a majority of the 71-member סנהדרין. If יאיר died at העי in יהושע's time, he lived through the desert, which strengthens the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally, exactly
About thirty (the 'כ' means 'like' or 'about')
Equal in worth to
The great court of 71 judges

phrases.english: And it was taught: literally thirty-six,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Nechemya said to him:
But does it say "thirty-six"?
Doesn't it say only "about thirty-six"!
Rather, this is Yair son of Menashe,
who was equal to the majority of the Sanhedrin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק cited in step 14 proves that יאיר survived the desert
steps.raayaObject: That יאיר בן מנשה was alive after ישראל entered the land
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי נחמיה's reading of 'כשלשים וששה' in יהושע 7:5 as referring to יאיר alone

steps.title: The decree did not cover anyone under twenty or over sixty
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב gives a new answer: the decree applied only to people between twenty and sixty. 'Under twenty' comes from the פסוק itself. 'Over sixty' is learned from the words 'and up' in the laws of ערכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא בר יעקב said: The decree was not made on anyone less than twenty or more than sixty. Not on less than twenty, as it is written 'from twenty years and up.' Not on more than sixty, because he learns 'and up' from 'and up' in ערכין. Just as there, over sixty is treated like under twenty, so too here, over sixty is treated like under twenty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets aside רב המנונא's answer and gives a new one. Only people between twenty and sixty were sentenced to die in the desert, so older men like יאיר could survive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of the decree says 'from twenty years and up,' which leaves out the young. The same words 'and up' appear in ערכין, where people over sixty are put in a separate group, just as people under twenty are. Linking the two פסוקים teaches that over-sixty was also left out of the decree. יאיר, born in יעקב's days, was far older than sixty, so he was spared.

keyTerms.meaning: The decree that the generation would die in the desert
And up (older)
He learns (one פסוק from another through shared words)
Valuations: the set amounts a person pledges to the בית המקדש, based on age

steps.confusionAlert: 'Over sixty is like under twenty' does not mean the two groups pay the same amount in ערכין. It only means both are outside the middle group of twenty to sixty, so both are outside the decree.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains how older people, and not only שבט לוי, could have lived from יציאת מצרים until after entering the land.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
The decree was not decreed
not on those less than twenty years old,
and not on those more than sixty years old.
Not on those less than twenty,
as it is written: "From twenty years old and up."
And not on those more than sixty,
he learns "and up" from "and up" in the laws of valuations;
phrases.notes: 'And up' also shows up in ויקרא 27:7, 'from sixty years and up', and the shared words link the two פסוקים.

phrases.english: just as there,

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר מִבֶּן שִׁשִּׁים כְּפָחוּת מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים,
phrases.english: more than sixty is like less than twenty,
so too here,

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר מִבֶּן שִׁשִּׁים כְּפָחוּת מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים.
phrases.english: more than sixty is like less than twenty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 14-15 by replacing רב המנונא's answer with a new age-based rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the limits of the decree by age
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every non-Levite adult was included in the decree, so יאיר and מכיר could not have survived
steps.terutzMaskana: Only those aged twenty to sixty were included, so people over sixty, like יאיר and מכיר, could survive
steps.whatToRemember: The decree to die in the desert covered only people aged twenty to sixty. 'Under twenty' comes from the פסוק itself, and 'over sixty' is learned from ערכין.

steps.title: Was the land divided by tribe or by head count?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: was ארץ ישראל split into equal shares for each tribe, or was land given per person, so that bigger tribes got more?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Was ארץ ישראל divided according to tribes, or perhaps divided according to the heads of the men?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a question it does not yet answer. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to divide the land. Each of the twelve tribes could get an equal share, or each man could get a share, which would make a big tribe's portion larger. The גמרא now wants to know which one the תורה meant.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them; opens an open question
Was divided
Perhaps
Literally 'skulls of men', meaning by head count

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Was Eretz Yisrael divided according to the tribes,
or perhaps it was divided according to the skulls of men?
phrases.notes: He means per person, so bigger tribes got more land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of who survived the desert ends
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ארץ ישראל was given in equal shares per tribe or in shares per person
